title: Grade 2 Math — Fri, Jun 27
description: Money — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — money word problems
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Which coin is worth the MOST?
questions.explanation: Among coins, ₹10 > ₹5 > ₹2 > ₹1. The ₹10 coin has the highest value.
₹50 + ₹50 = ₹100. Two fifty-rupee notes make one hundred rupees.

questions.question: You have ₹10 and buy a toy for ₹7. How much is left?
5 coins of ₹2 each = ?
questions.explanation: 5 × ₹2 = ₹10. Five two-rupee coins equal ten rupees.

questions.question: A ₹100 note is worth how many ₹50 notes?
questions.explanation: ₹100 ÷ ₹50 = 2. One hundred rupees equals two fifty-rupee notes.

questions.question: Asha has ₹20. She gives her friend ₹8. How much does Asha have left?
A juice costs ₹15. You give ₹20. What change do you get?
questions.explanation: ₹20 − ₹15 = ₹5. You get five rupees as change.

questions.question: Ravi has 3 notes of ₹10 and 2 coins of ₹5. How much money does he have in all?
A shop sells pencils at ₹3 each. How much do 4 pencils cost?
questions.explanation: 4 × ₹3 = ₹12. Four pencils at three rupees each cost twelve rupees.

questions.question: Sonu has ₹50. He spends ₹22 on a book and ₹8 on a pen. How much is left?
Which amount is GREATER — 2 notes of ₹20 or 5 coins of ₹10?
questions.explanation: 2 × ₹20 = ₹40. 5 × ₹10 = ₹50. So five ₹10 coins (₹50) is more than two ₹20 notes (₹40).

questions.question: A girl paid ₹100 for a dress and got ₹30 back. What was the price of the dress?
questions.explanation: Price = ₹100 − ₹30 = ₹70. The dress cost seventy rupees.

questions.question: Meenu saves ₹10 every day for a week (7 days). How much has she saved?
questions.explanation: 7 × ₹10 = ₹70. Saving ₹10 each day for 7 days gives ₹70 in total.

questions.question: Arjun has ₹75. He buys a toy for ₹48 and gives ₹10 to his sister. How much does he have left?
A shop has: mango ₹15, papaya ₹20, guava ₹12. You want to buy all three but have only ₹45. Do you have enough?
questions.explanation: Total = ₹15 + ₹20 + ₹12 = ₹47. You have ₹45 so you are ₹2 short.
